title: Pinnacle Paradigm Shift
headline: The outcome leads. The whole system follows.
description: Start with the abilities a child needs for self-sufficiency and mainstream participation. Then connect every assessment, specialist, technique and review to that direction.
comparisonNote: These comparisons describe disconnected and connected models of care; provider practices vary. The vehicle metaphor illustrates how the parts of a care system work together.

mission.text: Children, parents and families Pinnacle aims to empower through its stated mission.

evidenceNote: These nine perspectives explain the architecture supporting Pinnacle's seven-stage developmental approach. Linked records distinguish programme descriptions, licensed functions and research evidence. PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 is licensed for non-diagnostic developmental support, ages 0–12. Individual goals, support and outcomes vary.

title: You wanted the car.
Not a box of parts.
cards.eyebrow: FROM SEPARATE PARTS TO A WHOLE SYSTEM
cards.lead: The shift is in the architecture: measurement, planning, professional care, home practice and review working as one connected system.
cards.disconnected: When each service operates separately, the family may be left to assemble the bigger plan.
cards.connected: PinnacleAI® connects measurement, a child-specific record, coordinated support, everyday practice and review around a direction for self-sufficiency and mainstream participation.
cards.lifeMeaning: The whole system needs a destination from the first conversation.
cards.sourceNote: BIS schedule p. 2 names Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion; the dossier describes the connected care model. The vehicle is a planning metaphor.
cards.shareText: You wanted the car. Not a box of parts. PinnacleAI® connects measurement, plans, people, practice and review into one developmental-support approach. The difference is how it all works together.
cards.posterDisconnected: Separate services. The family assembles the plan.
cards.posterConnected: One child-specific system connects care, practice and review.
cards.posterMeaning: A direction toward self-sufficiency, mainstream participation and a wonderful life.
cards.description: The shift is in the architecture: measurement, planning, professional care, home practice and review working as one connected system.
cards.artworkDescription: Poster with manually typeset text over AI-generated conceptual artwork. It does not depict a real patient or document a clinical outcome.

title: Separate reports.
A shared starting point.
cards.eyebrow: FROM ISOLATED FINDINGS TO AN ABILITY BASELINE
cards.lead: A common ability framework gives each part of care a reference point for the same child.
cards.disconnected: When reports use separate reference points, their findings may be difficult to connect into shared priorities.
cards.connected: AbilityScore® brings Pinnacle's 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills into a structured starting point for discussing priorities across care.
cards.lifeMeaning: A shared baseline helps connect decisions across the system.
cards.sourceNote: Company walkthrough p. 26; September handout pp. 5–6. These are Pinnacle-defined framework layers. The dossier describes clinical assessment under professional governance.
cards.shareText: Separate reports need a shared starting point. Pinnacle's AbilityScore® framework brings 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills into a structured reference for care priorities.
cards.posterDisconnected: Reports that lack a shared starting point.
cards.posterConnected: AbilityScore® connects 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills.
cards.posterMeaning: A common baseline for connected decisions.
cards.description: A common ability framework gives each part of care a reference point for the same child. Read the connected-care comparison and its source records.

title: One child.
One continuing record.
cards.eyebrow: FROM PROVIDER PLANS TO A CHILD-SPECIFIC RECORD
cards.lead: Continuity needs a record that connects measurements, goals, context and responses across successive plans.
cards.disconnected: When each provider holds a separate plan, useful history may not inform the next recommendation.
cards.connected: The Personal Development Kernel retains the child's measurements, goals, environment and responses, giving subsequent recommendations a connected developmental history.
cards.lifeMeaning: The next plan can build on what the system already knows.
cards.sourceNote: Evidence Dossier pp. 48–49; methodology preprint p. 3. These describe the child-specific record informing subsequent recommendations.
cards.shareText: One child. One continuing record. Pinnacle's Personal Development Kernel connects measurements, goals, context and responses so successive plans can build on the child's history.
cards.posterDisconnected: Provider plans that lose the child's earlier history.
cards.posterConnected: The Personal Development Kernel keeps history, goals and responses connected.
cards.posterMeaning: Continuity from one plan to the next.
cards.description: Continuity needs a record that connects measurements, goals, context and responses across successive plans. Read the connected-care comparison and its source…

title: Many specialists.
One shared direction.
cards.eyebrow: FROM HANDOFFS TO COORDINATED PROFESSIONAL CARE
cards.lead: Expertise becomes a connected system when the people involved can work from shared goals and context.
cards.disconnected: If a handoff passes the child along without shared goals, coordination may depend on the family carrying every detail.
cards.connected: Pinnacle's model connects appropriate multidisciplinary therapies, parents, caregivers and educators around a child-specific plan, supported by professional judgement and human oversight.
cards.lifeMeaning: Each professional contribution can support the same developmental direction.
cards.sourceNote: MD-5 intended-use annexure names parents, therapists, educators and caregivers; September handout pp. 5–7 describes the programme; the dossier describes human oversight.
cards.shareText: Many specialists. One shared direction. Pinnacle's model connects multidisciplinary care, family observations and professional judgement around a child-specific plan.
cards.posterDisconnected: Handoffs without shared goals or context.
cards.posterConnected: A coordinated team works from one child-specific direction.
cards.description: Expertise becomes a connected system when the people involved can work from shared goals and context. Read the connected-care comparison and its source records.

title: Beyond the session.
A connected programme.
cards.eyebrow: FROM APPOINTMENT BOUNDARIES TO GUIDED PRACTICE
cards.lead: A connected programme carries agreed goals beyond the appointment, with practical guidance for the people supporting the child.
cards.disconnected: If the programme stops at the session door, home practice may lack a clear connection to the professional plan.
cards.connected: Everyday Therapy™ describes 7–9 selected daily techniques, connecting guided home practice with the child's abilities, goals and professional support.
cards.lifeMeaning: Home practice becomes a connected part of the programme.
cards.sourceNote: September handout pp. 5–7 describes 7–9 daily techniques. The individual programme determines appropriate activities; the MD-5 includes parents and caregivers as intended users.
cards.shareText: Beyond the session. A connected programme. Pinnacle's Everyday Therapy™ describes 7–9 selected daily techniques that connect guided home practice with the child's goals and professional support.
cards.posterDisconnected: A session plan without a connected home programme.
cards.posterConnected: Guided home practice connects 7–9 daily techniques with agreed goals.
cards.posterMeaning: The programme continues beyond the appointment.
cards.description: A connected programme carries agreed goals beyond the appointment, with practical guidance for the people supporting the child.
cards.artworkDescription: Poster with manually typeset text over AI-generated conceptual artwork. It does not depict a real patient or document a clinical outcome.

title: Close the feedback loop.
Review. Correct. Repeat.
cards.eyebrow: FROM SILOED OBSERVATIONS TO FUSION FEEDBACK
cards.lead: A system needs a way to bring observations back into decisions about activities, support and the next plan.
cards.disconnected: When observations remain in separate conversations or records, important feedback may never reach the next planning decision.
cards.connected: The Fusion Module links family and professional tracking with review and correction, helping the care team adjust activities or support.
cards.lifeMeaning: Feedback becomes an input to the next decision.
cards.sourceNote: BIS schedule p. 2 names tracking and correction; methodology preprint p. 3 describes activity feedback; dossier pp. 48, 52–53 describes human oversight.
cards.shareText: Close the feedback loop. Pinnacle's Fusion Module connects family and professional observations with tracking, review and correction, so feedback can inform the next planning decision.
cards.posterDisconnected: Observations that never reach the next planning decision.
cards.posterConnected: Fusion links feedback, professional review and plan correction.
cards.description: A system needs a way to bring observations back into decisions about activities, support and the next plan. Read the connected-care comparison and its source…

title: Tasks with a purpose.
Participation in view.
cards.eyebrow: FROM TASK TARGETS TO FUNCTIONAL GOALS
cards.lead: Holding a pencil can be one target. Participating in a classroom activity gives that target a wider purpose.
cards.disconnected: If completing a task becomes the endpoint, the plan may miss how that ability supports participation.
cards.connected: Pinnacle's pathway connects selected skills with goals for communication, daily living, learning and participation across its readiness framework.
cards.lifeMeaning: The activity and its purpose belong in the same plan.
cards.sourceNote: BIS schedule p. 2 names school readiness, self-sufficiency and mainstream inclusion. The pencil example illustrates a possible goal; it is not a reported patient outcome.
cards.shareText: Tasks with a purpose. Participation in view. Holding a pencil can support a classroom goal. Pinnacle's readiness approach connects selected skills with a wider developmental direction.
cards.posterDisconnected: Task completion without a clear link to participation.
cards.posterConnected: Selected skills connect with functional goals across the readiness framework.
cards.posterMeaning: A pencil task can support classroom participation.
cards.description: Holding a pencil can be one target. Participating in a classroom activity gives that target a wider purpose. Read the connected-care comparison and its source…

title: A plan that evolves.
Eight views to review.
cards.eyebrow: FROM AN UNCHANGED PLAN TO SCHEDULED REASSESSMENT
cards.lead: A connected system has a review cycle: compare the child's present abilities, reconsider priorities and explain what should change next.
cards.disconnected: Without scheduled reassessment, a plan may continue without a clear comparison of what has changed.
cards.connected: Pinnacle describes monthly reassessment, supported by eight report types: an overall AbilityScore® and seven readiness views for discussion and planning.
cards.lifeMeaning: The review feeds the next version of the plan.
cards.sourceNote: Monthly review: walkthrough pp. 35, 37 and methodology preprint p. 3. Readiness modules: BIS p. 2. Eight supplied report formats reviewed 19 September 2026.
cards.shareText: A plan that evolves. Eight views to review. Pinnacle describes monthly reassessment, with an overall AbilityScore® and seven readiness report types informing the next planning conversation.
cards.posterDisconnected: Plans that continue without scheduled reassessment.
cards.posterConnected: Monthly reassessment. AbilityScore® plus seven readiness views inform the next plan.
cards.posterMeaning: Review changes. Reconsider priorities. Adapt the plan.
cards.description: A connected system has a review cycle: compare the child's present abilities, reconsider priorities and explain what should change next.

title: Beyond more sessions.
A direction for transition.
cards.eyebrow: FROM OPEN-ENDED ACTIVITY TO READINESS REVIEW
cards.lead: A developmental system needs a direction for what comes next: school participation, growing independence and the support that makes them possible.
cards.disconnected: If session counts are the main measure, the direction for readiness, transition and continuing support may remain unclear.
cards.connected: Pinnacle's model uses readiness review to guide next steps toward school participation, self-sufficiency and mainstream inclusion, with appropriate continuing support.
cards.lifeMeaning: Readiness gives the plan a direction beyond the next appointment.
cards.sourceNote: BIS schedule p. 2 names the readiness indexes; the dossier describes the developmental direction. MD-5 scope is ages 0–12. Transition goals include appropriate continuing support.
cards.shareText: Beyond more sessions. A direction for transition. Pinnacle's readiness approach keeps school participation, self-sufficiency and mainstream inclusion in view, with appropriate continuing support.
cards.posterDisconnected: More sessions without a clear direction for transition.
cards.posterConnected: Readiness guides the next step toward inclusion, with appropriate support.
cards.posterMeaning: Keep readiness, transition and continuing support in view.
cards.description: A developmental system needs a direction for what comes next: school participation, growing independence and the support that makes them possible.
